A global livestock virome catalog links viruses with resistome assembly
abstractText: Abstract Livestock manure is a prominent One Health setting for antimicrobial resistance (AMR), yet the contribution of viruses to resistome assembly remains unresolved. Here we compile the Livestock Manure Virus Database (LMVD), a global catalog of 1,330,372 viral operational taxonomic units reconstructed from 4,017 metagenomes. Livestock manure viral communities exhibit restricted biogeographic distributions, and antibiotic use and farming scale show the highest relative predictive importance for viral diversity. Viral genomes contained 78 antibiotic resistance gene (ARG) subtypes, representing 9.1% of resistome diversity in livestock manure, but virus-encoded ARGs were infrequent. Bacteriophages instead showed extensive predicted links to bacterial hosts, with nearly all antibiotic-resistant bacteria linked to viruses, predominantly temperate viruses, and enrichment in pathogenic antibiotic-resistant bacteria. Together, these findings place bounds on the contribution of viruses to direct ARG dissemination and indicate that lysogenic interactions with resistant hosts may shape AMR risk.

title: Machine Learning Prediction of Transport Properties in Amorphous Polymer Electrolytes Using Chemically Informed Structural Descriptors
abstractText: Abstract Amorphous polymer electrolytes are promising candidates for next-generation lithium batteries. They offer improved safety and mechanical stability compared to conventional liquid electrolytes. However, predicting their transport performance remains challenging. Ionic conductivity and diffusivity depend on complex, coupled interactions between polymer structure, chemistry, and ion dynamics. This work leverages machine learning to predict four key transport properties in amorphous polymer electrolytes using a molecular dynamics data set of more than 6,000 polymer electrolyte systems. These are ionic conductivity, bis(trifluoromethanesulfonyl)imide (TFSI) diffusivity, lithium-ion diffusivity, and polymer diffusivity. To enhance predictive capability and preserve mechanistic interpretability, we engineered chemically and structurally meaningful features from Simplified Molecular-Input Line-Entry System (SMILES) representations. Selected features include elemental composition, functional group densities, polarity descriptors, and polymer flexibility metrics. Three modeling frameworks were trained and evaluated under 5-fold cross-validation, including random forest, gradient boosting, and neural networks. The neural network achieved the highest predictive performance across all four targets and exceeded prior benchmarks on three of them. It also exhibited substantially greater robustness to data partitioning than the tree-based baselines. Feature importance analysis was performed using both impurity-based rankings and Shapley additive explanations. Polymer backbone flexibility, polarity, and ionic environment were found to dominate transport behavior. Directional attribution further identified primary and secondary amines and carboxylate groups as specific negative contributors to lithium-ion mobility. The results of this work demonstrate that chemically informed structural descriptors can effectively predict electrolyte performance while yielding mechanistic insight. This enables accelerated screening and design of high-efficiency polymer electrolytes for future energy storage applications.

title: Are elite IPF powerlifters getting younger? Temporal trends in peak performance age and age at first recorded competition using OpenIPF data
abstractText: Abstract Background Whether elite International Powerlifting Federation (IPF) classic powerlifters are becoming younger and whether this reflects earlier recorded competition or a younger active population is unclear. This study examined temporal patterns in age, performance and recorded intervals to elite performance. Methods Population and top-100 analyses covered 2013 to 2025 and Open World Championship podium analyses covered 2013 to 2026. Earlier OpenIPF records informed competition histories. Population-wide age-performance relationships were estimated using locally weighted scatterplot smoothing and profile-cluster bootstrapping. Trends in annual medians were evaluated using Theil-Sen slopes and Kendall tests. Intervals from first recorded eligible competition to first observed elite performance were calculated among profiles with eligible histories. Results The performance cohort comprised 431,476 entries from 161,073 profiles. The population-wide curve peaked at 26.0 years (95% confidence interval [CI]: 25.4–26.5). Active-profile median age ranged from 23.5 to 25.0 years and showed no clear trend (0.00 years/year; 95% CI: −0.10 to 0.00; Kendall p = 0.173). Population median age at first recorded eligible Raw three-lift competition declined slightly (− 0.097 years/year; 95% CI: −0.200 to 0.000; Kendall p = 0.0085). Among 1,303 yearly top-100 profile-years and 602 podium observations, median age slopes were − 0.20 years/year (95% CI: −0.29 to − 0.10; Kendall p = 0.002) and − 0.37 years/year (95% CI: −0.50 to − 0.19; Kendall p = 0.001), respectively. Median IPF Goodlift Points increased by 1.21 (95% CI: 1.08–1.43; Kendall p < 0.001) and 1.52 points/year (95% CI: 1.33–1.79; Kendall p < 0.001), respectively. Median age at first recorded eligible Raw or Single ply three-lift competition showed no clear trend among top-100 profiles (0.00 years/year; 95% CI: −0.05 to 0.00; Kendall p = 0.289) or podium profiles (− 0.05 years/year; 95% CI: −0.22 to 0.00; Kendall p = 0.121). Raw-only elite histories showed negative first-competition-age trends. Median recorded intervals were 3.58 years for top-100 profiles and 4.72 years for podium profiles, with no clear temporal shortening. Conclusions Median age in elite samples declined while performance increased, whereas active-profile median age showed no clear decline. These descriptive findings provide updated age and performance benchmarks without establishing individual peak ages or faster progression to elite performance.

title: Robust and Scalable LPWAN Architecture with Integrated Security for Industrial IoT Applications
abstractText: Industrial Internet of Things (IIoT) is revolutionizing the means of critical infrastructure through real-time monitoring, automation and making smart decisions. The Low-Power Wide-Area Networks (LPWANs) like LoRaWAN, Sigfox, and NB-IoT are highly essential in enabling low energy, long-range two-way communication in IIoT-related use cases. Nevertheless, current implementations of LPWAN usually have serious gaps related to scalability, robustness, and security applied in an industrial world. In this study, a powerful and scalable framework of LPWAN is suggested combined with lightweight, multiple-layered security solutions depending on the specific requirements of IIoT communication. The framework provides hierarchical and intelligent adaptive network topography, dynamic clustering and intelligent gateway coordination. Its security is enforced by using symmetric encryption, key exchange on Elliptic curve and Device authentication using HMAC. Scalability and resilience are achieved by the architecture by incorporating adaptive channel allocation, fault-tolerant routing, and anomaly detection with edge intelligence in real-time. NS-3 simulation-based assessment with realistic industrial traffic patterns shows that a packet delivery ratio is more than 95 percent, latency reduces by up to 40 percent in crowded settings, and cryptographic overheads are less than 5 percent. The offered solution enhances the resistance to seemingly typical IIoT attacks (jamming, replay, node impersonation, etc.) considerably without affecting energy and latency consumption. The resultants substantiate the architecture in its ability to support secure and scalability of IIoTs and further research will integrate the architecture with real-life applicative industrial testbeds and blockchain efficient trust mechanisms.

title: Clade-specific transmission dynamics of enterovirus D68 and their association with acute flaccid myelitis
abstractText: Abstract Enterovirus D68 (EV-D68) is a common cause of mild respiratory illness in children but is also linked to acute flaccid myelitis (AFM), a rare and severe neurological condition which can result in permanent paralysis. Tracking EV-D68 transmission is difficult because symptoms overlap with other common childhood illnesses, making case reporting unreliable. As a result, the burden of EV-D68 transmission remains poorly understood, particularly prior to the first widely recognised outbreak in 2014. Phylodynamic approaches offer a powerful alternative to case-based surveillance, inferring epidemiological parameters directly from pathogen genetic sequences. Here we show, using a birth-death-sampling phylodynamic model applied to publicly available EV-D68 sequences from the 1990s to 2023 collected in Europe and North America, that seasonal EV-D68 transmission was well established long before the 2014 outbreak brought the virus to widespread attention. Furthermore, we show that AFM case burden is strongly associated with the transmission dynamics of a specific EV-D68 clade, clade B, an association not seen for clades A and D. These findings suggest that clade-specific biological differences drive AFM risk, with important implications for surveillance prioritisation and the timing of future burden of neurological disease.

title: BEYOND THE CLASSROOM: ANALYZING THE FACTORS AFFECTING GRADE 12 LEARNERS’ COLLEGE COURSE PREFERENCES
abstractText: This study utilized a quantitative descriptive-survey and correlational-predictive research design to systematically examine the variables dictating the college preferences of graduating senior high school learners. Conducted at Mindanao State University - Lanao National College of Arts and Trades (MSU-LNCAT) during the School Year 2025–2026, the investigation relied on a total seventy-three Grade 12 learner-respondents comprising of forty-three Humanities and Social Sciences Learner-respondents (58.90%) and thirty TVL track learner-respondents (41.10%), with a demographic concentration of fifty-six females (76.71%) and seventeen males (23.29%). Data was gathered via face-to-face classroom administration using a structured 5-point Likert scale questionnaire evaluating three predictive dimensions: Intrinsic Motivation, Familial Influence, and Peer Dynamics and Social Media Influence. Descriptive and inferential statistical treatments was used including frequency, percentage, weighted mean, standard deviation, item ranking, and the Pearson (r) Correlation Coefficient. Intrinsic Motivation emerged as the primary driver, yielding a high composite mean of 3.92 (High Influence) and a Significant Strong Positive Relationship, with course preferences, successfully rejecting the null hypothesis. Conversely, external factors had minimal impact; Familial Influence acted strictly as a secondary, consultative reference point with a neutral composite mean of 3.39 (Moderate Influence) and a weak, variable correlation, while Peer Dynamics and Social Media Influence exerted the weakest pressure, finishing with a low composite mean of 2.68 (Low Influence) and No Significant Relationship. Ultimately, these findings demonstrate that modern Grade 12 learner-respondents at MSU-LNCAT exercise high psychological autonomy, systematically prioritizing internal passion and specialized tracking competencies over parental expectations, peer circles, or digital trends.

title: Histidine-51 Facilitates the Conformational Change and Deprotonation of Horse Liver Alcohol Dehydrogenase–NAD+ Complexes
abstractText: Abstract Structural studies suggest that His-51 in wild-type horse liver alcohol dehydrogenase (ADH1E) facilitates proton transfer between the hydroxyl group of a ligand bound to the catalytic zinc and bulk solvent. Previous work showed that the Gln-51 substitution increases the pK values for pH dependencies for various enzymatic reactions by about 1.5 units, and stopped-flow studies on the binding of NAD+ and pyrazole suggested that the equilibrium position for the global conformational change of the enzyme–NAD+ complex became disfavored by 1000-fold. That conclusion needed confirmation. Here, X–ray crystallography of six ternary complexes of H51Q ADH with NAD+ and pyrazole, caprate, 2,2,2-trifluoroethanol, or 2,3,4,5,6-pentafluorobenzyl alcohol, and NADH and water or N-cyclohexylformamide shows that all complexes have the same closed conformation as wild-type ADH. Gln-51 fits in the region occupied by His-51 and does not affect the positions of bound coenzymes or inhibitors that coordinate to the catalytic zinc. Stopped-flow studies show that the rate-limiting formation of ternary complexes with H51Q ADH and NAD+ depends upon deprotonation of the ligands that bind to the catalytic zinc (pyrazole or 2,2,2-trifluoroethanol). Furthermore, the binding of NAD+ and trifluoroethanol monitored by fluorescence and proton release show that the H51Q substitution disfavors the conformational change by about 3-fold as compared to wild-type ADH. The pK values of the enzyme–NAD+ complexes with water and other zinc ligands increase because His-51 no longer facilitates the deprotonation. The roles of the zinc-water and His-51 in the mechanism are exposed.

title: ESTIMATING DAILY SOLAR IRRADIATION FROM SUNSHINE DURATION ACROSS THE SAHARA–SAHEL GRADIENT OF NIGER: AN ÅNGSTRÖM–PRESCOTT SCENARIO ASSESSMENT
abstractText: Ground-based irradiance measurements are almost absent in Niger, so photovoltaic (PV) planning relies on satellite or reanalysis products or on sunshine-duration proxies. This study estimates daily global horizontal irradiation (Rs) from ten years (2015–2024) of daily sunshine-duration records at three synoptic stations spanning the Sahara–Sahel gradient (Bilma, Agadez Aéro and N’Guigmi), using the Ångström–Prescott model applied at daily resolution with generic coefficients (a = 0.25, b = 0.50). A documented quality-control pass resolved duplicated monthly records, excluded values entered under non-existent dates and capped five marginal cases in which sunshine duration exceeded the astronomical day length. Coefficient uncertainty was represented by a scenario envelope (a = 0.20–0.30, b = 0.40–0.60) rather than a statistical interval. The central annual mean Rs was 5.57, 5.99 and 6.03 kWh m−2 d−1 at Agadez, Bilma and N’Guigmi, respectively. Monthly climatological means ranged from 4.64 to 6.61 kWh m−2 d−1, whereas the coefficient scenarios shifted the annual means between 4.46 and 7.24 kWh m−2 d−1. The June–August minimum of sunshine fraction was negatively associated with maximum relative humidity at Agadez (r = −0.53) and N’Guigmi (r = −0.69) but not at Bilma (r = +0.20), suggesting a different control at the Saharan station. The clearness index is shown to be an algebraic rescaling of the same input and is reported only as a diagnostic. The estimates are internally consistent but uncalibrated and unvalidated; a validation protocol against satellite and reanalysis products is specified.

title: Strategi Komunikasi Pemasaran melalui Influencer dalam Meningkatkan Brand Awareness
abstractText: Persaingan ketat di industri kedai kopi telah mendorong bisnis untuk mengembangkan strategi komunikasi pemasaran yang efektif untuk memperkuat kesadaran merek di tengah derasnya arus informasi digital. Salah satu pendekatan yang banyak diadopsi adalah penggunaan influencer melalui platform media sosial. Studi ini menganalisis implementasi Model AISAS (Attention, Interest, Search, Action, Share) melalui influencer sebagai strategi komunikasi pemasaran yang diterapkan oleh Hardi Kopi and Eatery untuk meningkatkan kesadaran merek. Penelitian ini menggunakan pendekatan kualitatif dengan metode studi kasus. Data dikumpulkan melalui wawancara mendalam, observasi, dan dokumentasi, dan selanjutnya dianalisis melalui reduksi data, penyajian data, dan penarikan kesimpulan. Validitas data dipastikan melalui triangulasi sumber dan metodologi. Hasil penelitian menunjukkan bahwa strategi komunikasi pemasaran berbasis influencer telah diimplementasikan sesuai dengan tahapan Model AISAS. Influencer menarik perhatian audiens melalui konten visual yang menyoroti suasana dan fasilitas kedai kopi, membangkitkan minat dengan menyajikan pengalaman otentik, mendorong audiens untuk mencari informasi lebih lanjut, memengaruhi keputusan mereka untuk berkunjung, dan memotivasi mereka untuk berbagi pengalaman di media sosial. Penerapan strategi-strategi ini telah berkontribusi pada peningkatan kesadaran merek Hardi Kopi and Eatery, mencapai tingkat Pengenalan Merek dan Pengingatan Merek, meskipun belum mencapai tingkat Top-of-Mind.

Antifibrinolytic Agent: Synthesis and Characterization of Cocrystal and Salts of Tranexamic Acid
abstractText: Abstract Tranexamic acid (TXA) is a potent antifibrinolytic agent with poor oral bioavailability (∼35–40%) due to its high polarity and zwitterionic nature, while physicochemical factors, including its structural instability, further hinder its absorption. In this study, the crystal engineering concept is applied to enhance the physicochemical properties of TXA through targeted structural modifications, resulting in the synthesis of pharmaceutically stable cocrystal and salt forms. The application of supramolecular synthon design, pKa rule, and structural geometry (molecular mimicry), resulted in the rational design, synthesis, and structural characterization of eight binary multicomponent forms of TXA: a TXA-adipate salt, monoclinic space group P21/n; a TXA-salicylate salt, monoclinic space group P21/n; a TXA-picolinate salt, monoclinic space group P21/c; a TXA-acetaminophen cocrystal hydrate, monoclinic space group P21; a TXA-malonate salt, orthorhombic space group Pbca; a TXA-maleate salt hydrate, monoclinic space group P21/c; a TXA-malate salt, monoclinic space group P21/c; and a TXA-citrate salt, triclinic space group P1̅ These multicomponent forms were obtained via different hydrogen bonding interactions, some of them charge-assisted (N–H···O, N+–H···O–, O–H···O, and O–H···O–) between NH2 and/or −OH groups of TXA and the carboxyl (−C(O−)═O) functional groups of the coformers. In the cocrystals, TXA exists as zwitterions (zero charge), whereas in the salts, it carries a positive charge due to the protonation of its carboxylic (−COOH) and ammonium (−NH3+) groups. The NH3+ to COO– charge-assisted H-bond provides stabilization to both the coformer COO– as well as the TXA’s NH3+. Solid-state characterization using Raman and FT-Raman spectroscopy, thermal techniques (DSC), and X-ray diffraction analysis (powder and single-crystal XRD) supports and confirms the structural novelty. The superior stability profiles of the new TXA cocrystal and salts under standard conditions (40 °C ± 2 °C, 75% ± 5% RH) establish an improved structure–property profile compared to pure TXA.

title: Optimalisasi Pengelolaan Data dan Layanan Administrasi Pendidikan melalui Pelatihan Pemanfaatan Google Workspace bagi Tenaga Kependidikan di Lingkungan Dinas Pendidikan Kota Bengkulu

A Comprehensive examination of the social, legal, and psychological dimensions of child marriage in Iran: a critical interpretive synthesis
abstractText: Abstract Background Child marriage in Iran is a complex phenomenon situated at the intersection of patriarchal structures, structural poverty, and legal ambiguity, resulting in profound physical and psychological trauma among affected women. Objective This study aims to identify and comprehensively synthesize the underlying determinants, lived consequences, and intervention strategies associated with child marriage in Iran through a critical interpretive synthesis of scientific, legal, and narrative literature. Methods A total of 118 scholarly sources, including quantitative and qualitative studies, jurisprudential-legal texts, historical analyses, and realist narrative accounts were reviewed. Data were analyzed using thematic synthesis and axial coding to identify recurring patterns in the contributing factors and consequences of this phenomenon. Findings The findings indicate that child marriage emerges from the convergence of three interrelated dimensions: poverty, the reproduction of traditional norms, and legal legitimization (Article 1041 of the Civil Code). At the psychological level, the phenomenon is associated with a loss of voice and agency, disruption of identity formation, and grief over a lost childhood. At the legal-religious level, a clear tension was identified between traditional jurisprudential rulings and contemporary requirements reflected, for instance, in principles such as the prohibition of harm ( ā -ḍ arar ) and rational repugnance underscoring the need for legal reform. Furthermore, an examination of coping strategies revealed that passive submission and constrained adaptation predominate among affected women. Among intervention approaches, narrative therapy and couple-therapy models (including approaches drawing on Emotionally Focused Therapy and Cognitive Behavioral Therapy) showed favorable outcomes in the individual studies reviewed, though the small number and limited comparability of these studies mean this synthesis cannot establish which approach is most effective, nor can it support population-level claims about marital dissolution rates. Conclusion Child marriage in Iran constitutes a structural and multidimensional social problem that is perpetuated through the subjugation and disempowerment of women. Addressing this phenomenon requires a multifaceted approach encompassing: (1) fundamental reform of Article 1041 of the Civil Code; (2) implementation of poverty-reduction and educational policies; and (3) specialized clinical interventions aimed at rebuilding the identity and attachment security of women affected by child marriage.

title: Cooperative Dual-Template Assembly of Bimodal Interconnected Mesoporous Carbon Nanospheres with Boosted Charge Transport
abstractText: Abstract Mesoporous materials have attracted great research attention since their first advent in 1990s; however, the self-assembly of soft micelles can generate only unary periodicity. A feasible strategy capable of building multinary pore structures remains scarcely explored due to huge synthetic difficulty. Herein, we explore a cooperative dual-template assembly route, which allows for compatible interaction of Pluronic P123 and L64 in solution, to successfully construct a type of mesoporous carbon nanospheres with bimodal mesopores. The key to such construction of hierarchical mesopores from a pure soft-template process without recruitment of a hard template mainly relies on the formation of composite micelles with both suitable mutual interactions and individually stabilized condensed states. The resultant mesoporous carbon spheres possess good uniformity in morphology and mesoporosity, including a mean particle size at ∼200 nm, a high surface area of 537 m2 g–1, and an interconnected bimodal mesopore size centered at 11.1 and 4.2 nm along with a massive amount of micropores. Moreover, this dual-template assembly strategy allows for precise structural regulation over the pore curvature and pore size through tailoring the reaction conditions. As a proof of concept, the fabricated bimodal mesoporous carbon, as an ammonium-ion battery anode, showcases excellent electrochemical performances owing to its permeable and gradient porous structure for fast mass and charge transfer. Our study underscores a facile and extendable toolbox for synthesizing complex or hierarchical mesostructures as advanced energy model materials.

Analisis Fenomenologi pada Pemain Melalui Hubungannya dengan Karakter Virtual dalam Game Online Genshin Impact
abstractText: Open-world online games such as Genshin Impact offer players freedom to explore virtual environments, interact with digital surroundings, and communicate with individuals from diverse cultural backgrounds. Thus, online gaming serves not only as entertainment but also as a digital space for social interaction, emotional experiences, moral negotiation, and identity development. This study aims to explore how Genshin Impact players understand their relationships with virtual characters, particularly regarding emotional attachment, moral values, and identity exploration and formation. A qualitative phenomenological approach was employed to examine players’ subjective experiences through in-depth interviews with five active Genshin Impact players. Data were analyzed interpretively by relating participants’ lived experiences to phenomenological perspectives on gaming, emotional attachment theories, Erikson’s identity versus role confusion framework, Bandura’s moral disengagement concept, and perspectives on gamer communities and virtual communication. The findings reveal that emotional attachment to virtual characters enables players to express idealized aspects of themselves, explore personal aspirations, and regulate emotions while distinguishing virtual experiences from reality. Players also negotiate moral values through automatic, reflective, and habitual moral disengagement processes, interpreting in-game actions according to the game’s normative and situational context. Furthermore, gaming communities strengthen social identity, interpersonal relationships, and belonging. Overall, online gaming can function as a digital space for self-reflection, social interaction, moral negotiation, and identity formation in contemporary life.

title: BEYOND TECHNOSTRESS AI Fatigue as a Cumulative Adaptation Burden in Education and Work
abstractText: Artificial intelligence has become a persistent layer of work and learning rather than an occasional tool. Users must repeatedly decide when to delegate, how to prompt, whether to trust, how to verify, and how responsibility should be distributed. This integrative review defines AI fatigue as a cumulative reduction in the cognitive, affective, or motivational capacity for adaptive AI engagement when interaction, evaluation, correction, learning, and role-adjustment demands accumulate faster than recovery and support. The review connects technostress, automation vigilance, cognitive load and offloading, trust calibration, digital fatigue, and the Job Demands–Resources perspective. It introduces an Exposure–Adaptation–Depletion–Response framework, a five-domain taxonomy, and an AI Fatigue Load model that separates use volume from uncertainty, task stakes, correction burden, interruption, role disruption, and imposed adoption velocity. The analysis is updated to incorporate a 2026 validated 15-item AI Fatigue Scale; the proposed load model complements that psychophysiological outcome measure by specifying socio-technical antecedents and exposure conditions. Educational and organizational applications show why AI may simultaneously improve output and worsen human sustainability. The article identifies recurring inferential errors, presents a measurement and longitudinal research agenda, and proposes an intervention hierarchy spanning interface design, workflow, curriculum, organizational policy, and governance. AI fatigue is positioned neither as generic screen tiredness nor as a synonym for burnout, but as an adaptation problem located in the coupled human–AI–institution system.

abstractText: Low student achievement is one of the problems in the learning process. This study aims to determine the effect of students’ perceptions of learning media and their motivation to learn on student achievement. The study used a quantitative method with an associative approach, with a sample of 93 students selected using total sampling. Data were collected using questionnaires and midterm exam scores, then analyzed using multiple linear regression. The results of the study indicate that students’ perceptions of instructional media do not have a significant effect on student learning outcomes (Sig. 0.114 > 0.05), learning motivation does not have a significant effect on student learning outcomes (Sig. 0.682 > 0.05), and students’ perceptions of instructional media and learning motivation, when considered simultaneously, do not significantly affect learning outcomes (Sig. 0.278 > 0.05). The coefficient of determination (R²) for learning was 2.8%, indicating that students’ perceptions of instructional media and learning motivation together contributed 2.8% to learning outcomes, while 97.2% is influenced by other factors outside the scope of this study. Thus, students’ learning outcomes in this study cannot yet be fully explained solely through students’ perceptions of instructional media and learning motivation. title: Topology-Dependent Hydrogen-Bond Cooperativity and Many-Body Stabilization in HSCN Oligomers
abstractText: Abstract Hydrogen-bond cooperativity plays a key role in determining the stability and properties of molecular aggregates, yet the influence of aggregation topology on its microscopic origin remains poorly understood for thiocyanic acid (HSCN). Here, the structural, energetic, electronic, and spectroscopic properties of HSCN oligomers (monomer–pentamer) with linear, ladder, and cyclic topologies were investigated using dispersion-corrected density functional theory. Interaction energy and many-body decomposition analyses show that aggregate stabilization is dominated by pairwise hydrogen-bond interactions, while cooperative many-body effects increase systematically with cluster size and are maximized in cyclic assemblies. Complementary QTAIM, NCI-RDG, and charge-density-difference analyses reveal progressive strengthening of the S–H···N hydrogen-bond network accompanied by enhanced intermolecular polarization, without altering its closed-shell character. These electronic signatures are consistently reflected in the vibrational spectra through systematic red shifts of the S–H stretching mode. Together, the energetic, real-space electronic, and spectroscopic results demonstrate that hydrogen-bond topology governs the emergence of cooperative stabilization in HSCN oligomers, with cyclic architectures providing the most effective framework for collective hydrogen-bond reinforcement.

title: Artificial Intelligence Applications in Pregnancy, Childbirth, and the Postpartum Period: A Scoping Review
abstractText: Background: The use of digital health technologies, such as chatbots and virtual assistants based on artificial intelligence, has grown significantly in maternal health. These tools have been applied at different stages of the pregnancy and postpartum cycle, with emphasis on health education, risk monitoring, breastfeeding support, and mental healthcare. Despite their potential, challenges remain regarding clinical effectiveness, equity of access, and ethical safety. The aim of this study was to map the available evidence regarding the applications of artificial intelligence in pregnancy, childbirth, and postpartum care, with particular emphasis on conversational agents, virtual assistants, machine learning models, and clinical decision support systems, as well as their potential benefits, limitations, ethical implications, and implementation challenges. Methods: A scoping review was conducted between August and September 2025 in PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, Nursing Database, Latin American and Caribbean Literature in Health Sciences, and Google Scholar. Original articles, reviews, experience reports, and theoretical reflections published in Portuguese, English, or Spanish that addressed the use of digital tools based on artificial intelligence in the pregnancy and postpartum cycle were included. The analysis of the studies was organized into five thematic axes: applications in prenatal care; support during childbirth; postpartum monitoring and breastfeeding; perinatal mental health; and ethical, technical, and implementation challenges. Results: The search identified 6230 records, of which 13 studies were included. Findings indicate that chatbots and virtual assistants show good acceptability, promote health education, and contribute to the early detection of physical and emotional risks. However, most of the studies are exploratory, with methodological limitations, lack of clinical trials, and limited validation in socially vulnerable contexts. Conclusions: Chatbots and artificial intelligence tools are promising resources for perinatal care, particularly as a complement to face-to-face attention. Their consolidation requires robust studies, cost-effectiveness assessments, and public policies that ensure equity and digital inclusion.

abstractText: لم يكن الخط الفاصل بين أهل السنة والشيعة في القرون الأولى بالحدّة التي هو عليها اليوم. ولذلك أمكن للراوي ذي الميول الشيعية أن يجد له موضعًا في مصادر أهل السنة ما دام لا يدعو إلى مذهبه، وكان العكس ممكنًا أيضًا. وتهدف هذه الدراسة إلى تتبّع الروايات على مستوى الإسناد لمعرفة هل انتقلت بين منظومتَي الرواية عند الطائفتين، وإن انتقلت ففي أيّ اتجاه وبأيّ طريق. وقد اختيرت عيّنةً للدراسة الرواياتُ المرقّمة من 20 إلى 29 في الباب المخصّص لفضائل علي بن أبي طالب (ت 40/661) من كتاب الموضوعات لابن الجوزي (ت 597/1201). وتُتُبّعت طرق هذه الروايات في المصادر السنية والشيعية باستعمال برنامجَي الشاملة ومكتبة أهل البيت، ورُسمت لكل رواية مخطّطات إسنادها. ومُيّزت في المخطّطات أسانيد المصنّفات الشيعية، ولم تُدخَل طبقة الصحابة في المقارنة. أما المصادر التي أوردت الرواية بلا إسناد فلم تُدرَج في المخطّطات. ودُرست تراجم الرواة الواقعين في نقاط التقاء طرق الإسناد في كتب الرجال عند الطائفتين، وموقعهم في كتب الرواية عندهما. وتقترح الدراسة لهذا الغرض ثلاثة مفاهيم. فملتقى البراديغم هو الراوي الذي تلتقي عنده لأول مرة في مخطّط الإسناد طرقٌ مختلفة الانتماء المذهبي. وراوي الانتقال هو الراوي الواقع في هذا الموضع، الذي له ترجمة مستقلة في المنظومة الرجالية لكلا البراديغمين، ويقوم بمهمة النقل في مصنّفات الرواية عند كليهما. وأما راوي الانتقال الصوري فهو الذي يقع في الملتقى ولكنه يفقد أحد هذين الشرطين على الأقل. ومن بين الملتقيات التسعة التي رُصدت في العيّنة لم يوجد راوي الانتقال إلا في ثلاثة منها. وهؤلاء هم أبو هارون العبدي والحارث بن حصيرة وعبيد الله بن موسى. وأما أكثر الملتقيات فهي من قبيل راوي الانتقال الصوري. ووقع الانتقال في بعض الروايات لا على مستوى الراوي، بل على مستوى المؤلف أو بانتقال نسخة من يد إلى يد. وفي إحدى الروايات يوجد راوي انتقال في الإسناد مع أنه لا ملتقى فيها. ولم يُعَدّ إيرادُ المصنّفين من أهل السنة روايةً لمجرّد بيان وضعها دليلًا على التداخل الروائي. وتُظهر الدراسة أن وجود الملتقى لا يدلّ بمفرده على التداخل الروائي. فالتداخل الروائي ظاهرة محدودة يمكن تتبّعها، تجري عبر رواة بأعيانهم ومصنّفات بعينها.

title: Multinuclearity Effect of Yb(III) Complexes as Sensitizers for Near-Infrared-to-Visible Triplet–Triplet Annihilation Upconversion
abstractText: Abstract NIR-to-visible upconversion (UC) has garnered substantial attention owing to its promising applications in biomedicine and solar energy conversion. Although organo-Yb(III) complexes as photosensitizers can overcome the threshold of large anti-Stokes shifts in NIR-to-visible UC based on triplet–triplet annihilation (TTA), improving the quantum yields remains a formidable challenge. Herein, focusing on the Yb3+-complex/Rubrene coupling that emits yellow light (λem = 560 nm) under NIR excitation (980 nm), we systematically investigate the multinuclearity effect induced by three Yb(III) complex sensitizers, namely, binuclear [Yb2(Salen)2(H2Salen)Cl2(MeOH)2] (Yb-1), trinuclear [Yb3(Salen)3(HSalen)(OH)2] (Yb-2), and tetranuclear [Yb4(Salen)4(NO3)2(CO3)(DMF)2] (Yb-3). The progression from binuclear to tetranuclear architecture systematically enhances 980 nm absorbance, suppresses nonradiative loss, and improves energy transfer efficiency, culminating in a maximal upconversion intensity for tetranuclear Yb-3 (absorbance = 28.6 M–1cm–1, UC energy transfer efficiency = 4.0%, relative intensity 1.67 times larger than Yb-1 and 1.25 times large than Yb-2). This work provides key insights for the rational design of high-performance Yb3+-complex/Rubrene TTA-UC systems.

title: NEGLECTED MONTEGGIA FRACTURE-DISLOCATION IN AN ADOLESCENT: CLOSED REDUCTION OF THE RADIAL HEAD FOLLOWING ULNAR OSTEOTOMY
abstractText: Neglected Monteggia fracture-dislocations represent a therapeutic challenge due to the difficulties associated with radial head reduction and restoration of elbow function. We report the case of a 16-year-old adolescent presenting with a Bado type I Monteggia fracture-dislocation that had remained untreated for three months following loss to follow-up. Clinical examination revealed limited elbow flexion and complete loss of forearm pronation and supination. Radiographs demonstrated ulnar malunion associated with persistent radial head dislocation. A transverse ulnar osteotomy followed by realignment and fixation with a dynamic compression plate (DCP) allowed indirect reduction of the radial head without surgical exposure of the joint. Temporary humeroradial pin fixation was performed to maintain the reduction. At the three-month postoperative follow-up, the patient showed a favorable outcome, with radiographic union of the ulnar osteotomy, maintained radiocapitellar alignment, and full recovery of elbow flexion-extension and forearm pronation-supination. This case highlights the feasibility of indirect radial head reduction following ulnar realignment in selected patients with neglected Monteggia injuries. However, the success of this approach depends on the anatomical characteristics of the injury and the reducibility of the radial head. Longer-term follow-up is required to assess the maintenance of reduction and the durability of functional recovery.

Ripples in Two-Dimensional Supports Direct Charge–Curvature Coupling in Donor–Acceptor Interfacial Chemistry
abstractText: Abstract Ripples, wrinkles, and bubbles are common out-of-plane distortion motifs in deformable two-dimensional (2D) materials. By reshaping electronic structure, these distortions introduce a design dimension for functional materials under external bias. Here, we establish the relationship between out-of-plane-distortion-induced curvature and external-bias-induced charge and show that variable curvature can generate chemically distinct donor–acceptor interfacial chemistry on a single surface. Using corrugated graphene-supported M–N4 single-atom sites, representative of transition-metal–nitrogen–carbon (M–N–C) materials used in heterogeneous and electrochemical catalysis, we examine how negative curvature (mountain) and positive curvature (valley) regions respond to electron- and hole-rich conditions relevant to external bias. We identify a metal-dependent charge–curvature relationship in which donor and acceptor binding exhibit complementary mountain–valley asymmetry, arising from the interplay between localized and delocalized electronic states. The same asymmetry extends to coadsorption, where donor and acceptor species preferentially occupy complementary curvature regions of the shared corrugated support, resulting in long-range charge redistribution across the coupled donor–support–acceptor interface. Overall, these results establish ripples as chemically active motifs for bias-controlled interfacial chemistry relevant to catalysis and optoelectronics.

title: Selective Hg2+ Detection Using an Aza-BODIPY-Derived NIR Fluorescence Sensor: Environmental and Biological Applications
abstractText: Abstract Mercury contamination in natural environments poses severe threats to ecosystems and human health, emphasizing the urgent need for reliable Hg2+ detection methods. In this work, a novel near-infrared (NIR) fluorescent aza-BODIPY derivative (BT) was synthesized as a potential fluorescence sensor. BT exhibited dual colorimetric and “turn-on” NIR fluorometric responses toward Hg2+ in H2O:EtOH (3:7 v/v), achieving a detection limit of 1.7 ppb. The sensor displayed high selectivity through rapid BT–Hg2+ complexation, with reversible sensing enabled by the addition of potassium iodide (KI). Practical applicability was demonstrated by quantifying Hg2+ in environmental water and fertilizer samples. BT-based paper test strips provided a specific colorimetric response for Hg2+, while bioimaging in human liver cancer cells revealed effective visualization with low cytotoxicity. Collectively, these findings establish BT as a versatile and reliable platform for Hg2+ detection, offering significant promise for environmental monitoring and sustainable health protection.

title: Development and Validation of an LC–MS/MS Method for Simultaneous Determination of Gamma-Aminobutyric Acid (GABA), Glutamic Acid, and Glutamine in Fermentation Supernatant
abstractText: Abstract A selective liquid chromatography–tandem mass spectrometry (LC–MS/MS) method was developed and validated for the simultaneous, derivatization-free determination of gamma-aminobutyric acid (GABA), glutamic acid, and glutamine in fermentation supernatant. This hydrophilic interaction liquid chromatography–MS/MS approach offers simplified sample preparation and simultaneous quantification of GABA with its metabolic precursors. Chromatographic separation was achieved on a Waters ACQUITY UPLC BEH Amide column, with internal standard normalization using isotopically labeled analogs (GABA-d2 and glutamic acid-d5) improving calibration robustness. Method validation following ICH Q2(R1) guidelines confirmed linearity (R2 ≥ 0.99; ≥0.9999 for GABA and glutamic acid with internal-standard normalization) over validated ranges of 4–70 μM (GABA), 1–100 μM (glutamic acid), and 1–9 μM (glutamine), limits of detection of 0.17–0.25 μM, lower limits of quantification of 1–4 μM, intra-day precision ≤7.9% RSD and inter-day precision ≤4.9% RSD for GABA and glutamic acid (between-day 10–17% RSD for glutamine, which, quantified without an isotopically labeled internal standard, is reported as a fit-for-purpose, semiquantitative measure), between-day accuracy within ±15% bias at every level except the glutamic acid lower limit of quantification, where the +18.6% bias falls within the ±20% criterion applicable at that level, and negligible carryover. The validated method was applied to quantify GABA, glutamic acid, and glutamine in fermentation supernatant from bacterial strains cultivated under various conditions. This practical analytical tool supports process optimization and quality control in microbial fermentation for functional food production. The contribution is the de novo development and ICH Q2(R1) validation of this established technique for MRS-based fermentation supernatant, including baseline resolution of GABA from its isobaric isomer α-aminobutyric acid, and its application across lactic-acid-bacteria fermentations.

title: From Critique to Paradigm: Husserl’s Appropriation of Riemannian Geometry
abstractText: Abstract This work offers a new interpretation of the intellectual dialogue between Edmund Husserl and Bernhard Riemann’s theory of manifolds, arguing that this relationship extends beyond mere influence to constitute a central structural inspiration of the project Husserl would later outline as pure logic in the Prolegomena to Pure Logic . The original contribution of this analysis is to demonstrate how Husserl’s engagement evolved from an initial critical opposition, centered on the accusation of a “vicious circle” in deriving Euclidean geometry, to the adoption of Riemann’s work as a crucial paradigmatic model for his own Doctrine of Manifolds ( Mannigfaltigkeitslehre ). The paper documents the overcoming of this critique, a turning point evidenced by Husserl’s distinction between the “pure categorial form” of the manifold and its “concretization” in phenomenal space. In doing so, Husserl found in the Riemannian separation between a manifold’s abstract topological structure and its metric the perfect model for his own distinction between the ideal form of a theory and its empirical content. Ultimately, we demonstrate how Husserl assimilated the structural potentials of Riemann’s mathematics to prefigure the three fundamental tasks of pure logic, therefore transforming a revolutionary mathematical structure into a primary paradigm for his transcendental theory of science.

title: Konsep Dasar Akhlak, Moral, Etika, dan Karakter serta Hakikat Pendidikan Akhlak
abstractText: Moral education (akhlak) is a fundamental component of Islamic education that aims to develop individuals with noble character based on the values of the Qur'an and Sunnah. In the development of modern education, the concept of akhlak is frequently associated with morality, ethics, and character. Although these four concepts are closely related to human behavior, each has distinct philosophical foundations, sources of values, and orientations. This study aims to examine the fundamental concepts of akhlak, morality, ethics, and character, as well as the essence of moral education from an Islamic perspective, through a library research approach. Data were obtained from the Qur'an, Hadith, classical Islamic texts, and contemporary literature on Islamic education. The findings indicate that akhlak is rooted in divine revelation and constitutes a primary objective of Islamic education, while morality develops from societal norms, ethics originates from philosophical inquiries into right and wrong, and character represents the integration of values that become embedded in individual habits. Furthermore, moral education in Islam is not merely oriented toward the transmission of knowledge but also emphasizes the transformation of individual personality through role modeling, habituation, guidance, supervision, and the internalization of Islamic values.

title: Integration of Human Factors Analysis and Classification System (HFACS) and Failure Mode and Effects Analysis (FMEA) In Fleet Traffic Accident Risk Analysis At PT Semen Indonesia Logistik
abstractText: Traffic accidents involving distribution fleets are a safety concern that can be influenced by human factors, environmental conditions, supervision, and organizational factors. This study aims to identify the factors contributing to traffic accidents and determine risk priorities as a basis for developing recommendations to improve fleet safety at PT Semen Indonesia Logistik. The methods used are the Human Factors Analysis and Classification System (HFACS) and Failure Mode and Effects Analysis (FMEA). HFACS is used to classify factors contributing to accidents, while FMEA is used to prioritize risks based on the Risk Priority Number (RPN). The integration of these methods enables the study not only to identify accident causation factors but also to determine which risks require the most immediate attention. The HFACS analysis shows that Adverse Mental States is the most dominant category, with 35 occurrences (18.92%), followed by Decision Errors with 33 occurrences (17.84%) and Perceptual Errors with 28 occurrences (15.14%). Meanwhile, the FMEA results indicate that driver fatigue has the highest RPN of 504, followed by failure to maintain a safe following distance with an RPN of 378 and failure to detect objects in blind spots with an RPN of 324. Based on these findings, the recommended improvements include implementing fatigue management, regulating working hours and rest periods, providing defensive driving training, increasing blind-spot awareness, and optimizing driving behavior monitoring. The integration of HFACS and FMEA can support the systematic identification of accident causation factors and the prioritization of risk control measures.

How ENSO controls the propagation speed of seasonal onsets in Java–Bali: satellite rainfall evidence over two decades
abstractText: Indonesia, as a tropical maritime continent, exhibits a seasonal rainfall pattern influenced by the El Niño–Southern Oscillation (ENSO). Variations in the Wet Season Onset (WSO) and Dry Season Onset (DSO) have broad implications for agriculture, water resources and disaster mitigation. This study aims to analyse the climatology and interannual variability of WSO and DSO over the Java–Bali region (104–116°E), using satellite-based rainfall data (1998–2024). The results show a clear monsoonal pattern, with maximum (minimum) rainfall from December to February (June to August). Climatologically, WSO (DSO) propagates eastward (westward) at ~21 km day–¹ (19 km day–¹) with an onset difference of ~57 (64) days between western Java and Bali. WSO is coherent across all four regions, whereas DSO is coherent across three Java regions (weaker coherence with Bali), consistent with a stronger and more spatially uniform ENSO relationship for WSO. Despite the ENSO predictability barrier, DSO remains significantly related to the Relative Oceanic Niño Index (RONI), with earlier DSO associated more strongly with the developing positive ENSO than with the decaying event from the preceding wet season. El Niño accelerates westward propagation of DSO, whereas La Niña slows DSO and WSO propagation. For WSO, El Niño delays the onset timing with propagation speed comparable with climatology, whereas La Niña advances onset with slower progression. Hence, ENSO affects seasonal onset timing and modulates the longitudinal propagation pace of monsoonal systems. These findings highlight monsoon spatio-temporal propagation as a key atmospheric response to ENSO over Java–Bali, with implications for climate prediction, agricultural planning and hydrometeorological risk management.

PILOMATRICOMA OF THE NECK IN EARLY CHILDHOOD: A CASE REPORT
abstractText: Pilomatricoma is a benign adnexal tumor arising from the hair follicle matrix, most commonly encountered in children. While typically presenting as a small superficial lesion, atypical forms in the cervical region may mimic malignant conditions and lead to diagnostic uncertainty. Case Presentation: We report the case of a 3-year-old child with a family history notable for the death of a sibling from lymphoma, who presented with a progressively enlarging posterior cervical mass. Clinical examination revealed a firm, partially hard, painless swelling without signs of inflammation. Given the clinical context, a malignant etiology was initially suspected. Cervical computed tomography (CT) demonstrated a well-defined subcutaneous mass with heterogeneous density and internal calcifications. To further characterize the lesion, cervical magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) was performed, confirming a well-circumscribed lesion without deep tissue invasion. The patient subsequently underwent complete surgical excision with a bloc resection of the mass. Histopathological examination established the diagnosis of pilomatricoma, revealing characteristic basaloid cells, ghost cells, and areas of calcification. Discussion: Pilomatricoma can present as a diagnostic challenge, particularly when located in the cervical region and associated with atypical features or an alarming clinical history. Imaging plays a key role, with calcifications on CT being a helpful clue, while MRI assists in assessing local extension. However, definitive diagnosis relies on histopathological examination. Awareness of this entity is crucial to avoid misdiagnosis and overly aggressive management. Conclusion: Pilomatricoma should be considered in the differential diagnosis of firm cervical masses in children, even in clinically concerning contexts. Complete surgical excision remains both diagnostic and curative.

Temporal dissociation of physiological adaptations during speaking valve training in tracheostomized patients: a wearable device-based study
abstractText: Abstract Background Speaking valve (SV) training facilitates communication and ventilator weaning for tracheostomized patients, yet the dynamic, multi-system physiological responses and their temporal trajectories remain poorly characterized. This study aims to comprehensively evaluate the cardiopulmonary adaptations during and following SV training using wearable sensing technology. Methods A prospective observational study was conducted on 120 tracheostomized patients. Continuous physiological monitoring was performed using a wearable sensor across three phases: baseline (T0), SV intervention (T1), and recovery (T2). A multidimensional panel of 86 parameters was extracted across four domains: macro vital signs, respiratory cycle structure, respiratory complexity, and heart rate variability (HRV). Results SV training was well-tolerated, with no participants meeting predefined safety stopping criteria. Analysis revealed a distinct temporal decoupling in physiological responses—that is, respiratory mechanical and autonomic adaptations occurred immediately during valve use, whereas oxygenation improvements emerged only after valve removal. During the intervention (T1 vs. T0), patients exhibited immediate respiratory mechanical adaptation and significantly enhanced respiratory complexity (increased multiscale entropy at scales1–5; adjusted p < 0.05), reflecting active neural compensatory regulation by the respiratory controller. This was accompanied by acute cardiovascular stress, evidenced by vagal withdrawal (decreased RMSSD, HF power, and total power). However, oxygenation metrics remained unchanged during T1. Notably, significant improvements in oxygenation (increased minimum SpO₂ and reduced desaturation burden) emerged exclusively during the recovery phase (T2 vs. T0; adjusted p < 0.05). Furthermore, autonomic recovery was delayed: the LF/HF ratio rose significantly from training to recovery ( p = 0.02), indicating persistent sympathetic predominance after valve removal. Conclusions SV training triggers an immediate respiratory regulation response and acute cardiovascular stress, whereas the beneficial effects on oxygenation manifest as a delayed phenomenon during recovery. This temporal decoupling underscores the necessity of incorporating monitored recovery periods into SV clinical protocols and highlights the value of multidimensional wearable monitoring in revealing covert physiological dynamics in critically ill patients.

title: Perceptual and Behavioral Determinants for Optimizing Energy Performance in Buildings: A Study of Maladaptive Human Interactions
abstractText: The persistent discrepancy between predicted and actual building energy performance has highlighted the need to better understand the role of occupants in shaping operational energy outcomes. While technological advances have significantly improved building efficiency, human behavior remains a critical yet often underestimated determinant of actual energy consumption. This study investigates the behavioral and environmental factors influencing lighting related energy use in office environments, with particular emphasis on environmental concern, flexibility of energy-control systems, and responsive occupant behavior. Drawing upon theories from environmental psychology, behavioral science, and architectural research, a mixed-method approach was adopted comprising naturalistic observations, structured behavioral observations, and a survey-based investigation. Fieldwork was conducted within contemporary office environments. Following exploratory observations across multiple workplaces, a case-study office building was selected for detailed investigation. The study involved 77 participants representing a range of professional roles, including administrators, engineers, programmers, and researchers. The findings indicate that environmental concern alone does not adequately explain adaptive energy related behavior. Instead, occupants’ responses emerge through the interaction of personal values, environmental opportunities, spatial perception, and the accessibility of environmental control systems. Flexible lighting-control mechanisms, including adjustable blinds and decentralized lighting controls, were found to encourage greater engagement with daylight and more responsive lighting-related actions. Conversely, social dynamics, workplace norms, and limited environmental control frequently constrained adaptive behavior despite occupants’ awareness of energy-saving opportunities. The study argues that occupants should be regarded as active participants in building performance rather than unpredictable sources of variation. The results demonstrate that improving building energy performance requires an integrated human-centered approach in which architectural design, environmental affordances, and behavioral determinants are considered alongside technological efficiency measures. By supporting environmental awareness, user autonomy, and adaptive interaction, buildings can more effectively reduce the performance gap and achieve long-term sustainability objectives.

abstractText: Fractions are among the most difficult topics for Indonesian students, yet empirical evidence on the GASING (Gampang, Asyik, dan Menyenangkan) method for this topic, particularly when examined by students’ Prior Mathematical Knowledge (PMK), remains limited. This study aimed to compare the fraction numeracy of seventh-grade students taught with the GASING method and those receiving direct instruction, and to describe the gain profile across PMK categories. A quasi-experimental nonequivalent pretest-posttest control group design was used with 48 students from two public junior secondary schools in Lembata Regency, East Nusa Tenggara (28 experimental, 20 control). Data were analysed using the Mann-Whitney U test, normalized gain (N-gain), and the Kruskal-Wallis test. Posttest scores of the GASING group were significantly higher than those of the direct instruction group (U = 123.5, p = .001, r = .48). Mean N-gain in the GASING group was high for high-PMK (g = 0.77) and low-PMK students (g = 0.75) and medium for medium-PMK students (g = 0.64), whereas all direct instruction subgroups showed medium gains (g = 0.44–0.65). Posttest scores also differed across PMK categories (χ²(2) = 6.39, p = .041, η²H = .10). Within the two schools studied, GASING yielded better fraction numeracy than direct instruction at all PMK levels, with the largest N-gain difference among low- and medium-PMK students. Larger samples are needed to test the method × PMK interaction inferentially.

title: Immunogenicity and Safety of PHH-1V COVID-19 Vaccine as a Heterologous Booster in Adolescents
abstractText: BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVES PHH-1V, a protein-based, non-mRNA, bivalent, adjuvanted COVID-19 vaccine, has demonstrated strong immunogenicity and favorable safety as a booster in adults. This study evaluated PHH-1V as a heterologous booster in adolescents. METHODS HIPRA-HH-3 was a phase IIb, open-label, multicenter, noninferiority trial assessing the immunogenicity and safety of PHH-1V in 240 healthy adolescents (≥ 12 to < 18 years) primed with BNT162b2. Immunogenicity (N = 90) was assessed by measuring neutralizing antibodies against SARS-CoV-2 variants and total binding antibodies in adolescent participants vs young adults (≥ 18 to ≤ 25 years) (N = 81) from a previous trial, who had also been boosted with PHH-1V. T-cell responses at day 14 post booster were also evaluated. Antibody durability and adverse events (AEs) were assessed through day 336. RESULTS Neutralizing titers—against Omicron BA.1 (primary endpoint), WH1, Beta, and Delta variants—and total binding antibodies were significantly higher in adolescents than in young adults (P < .001), demonstrating noninferiority (margin < 1.5). T-cell responses against BA.1 and Beta also increased significantly (P < .001). Cross-variant antibody titers remained above baseline (day 0) through day 336. AEs were mostly mild/moderate, primarily injection-site pain and headache within 28 days. No related serious AEs were reported. CONCLUSIONS As a heterologous booster in adolescents, PHH-1V is safe and elicits cellular and sustained humoral responses with cross-variant immune recognition, which support the use of PHH-1V in adolescent vaccination strategies. Data in younger and specific risk groups are still needed.

title: Radical–Electrochemical Coupling Enables Amination of Methane
abstractText: Abstract The selective functionalization of methane under ambient conditions is widely regarded as a holy grail in chemistry, yet remains fundamentally limited not only by the inertness of the C–H bond but also by the transient nature of highly reactive intermediates. Short-lived species are often difficult to preserve and utilize prior to productive coupling, constraining accessible reaction pathways and product selectivity. Here, we establish a reaction framework based on in situ interfacial interception of reactive radicals, enabling the temporal coordination between radical lifetime and subsequent reaction processes. Plasma generates short-lived methyl radicals in immediate proximity to a gas–electrode interface, allowing their direct delivery and capture at the catalytic surface, while the electrochemical interface independently converts ammonia into surface-bound amino intermediates. Their coupling enables selective C–N bond formation. This spatially and temporally coordinated process allows highly reactive radical species to be synchronized with interfacial reaction steps, facilitating their productive utilization. Guided by density functional theory, we identify a nickel–cobalt layered double hydroxide catalyst that promotes interfacial coupling between *CH3 and *NH2 intermediates. The optimized system achieves a Faradaic efficiency of 54% for methylamine at 10 mA cm–2, with a productivity of 201 μmol cm–2 h–1 under ambient conditions. Beyond methane amination, this work demonstrates that coordinating the lifetime and transformation of reactive intermediates provides a generalizable strategy for catalytic control, offering new opportunities for the activation and selective transformation of inert molecules.

On Ammonia-Blended Coke Oven Gas (COG) in Coaxial-Flow Nonpremixed Flame for Decarbonization
abstractText: Abstract Coke oven gas (COG) is a promising byproduct gas generated in steelmaking processes because of its high heating value and large production volume. The large amount of hydrogen in COG contributes to combustion reactivity, flame stability, and decarbonization. Recently, a strategy for recycling COG cofired with other fuels has been proposed to support continued utilization. Ammonia is an attractive carbon-free fuel, a suitable candidate for cofiring with COG. In this study, the combustion and emission characteristics of ammonia-blended COG were investigated using a coaxial-flow nonpremixed combustor. Experiments evaluated the flame length, blow-off limit, and OH radical and NOx emissions. 2D simulation using ANSYS Fluent analyzed flame temperature and NO mole fraction. As a result, it was found that the flame length decreased with increasing ammonia blending ratio because of the reduced heat release rate and fuel reactivity. The normalized correlation based on Roper’s equation accurately predicts the flame length of COG, implying that COG can subsequently be interpreted as a general-purpose fuel. In addition, despite decreased blow-off limit of the ammonia-blended COG, it still maintained a significantly higher stability limit than methane due to the high hydrogen content of COG. OH-PLIF measurements revealed that the flame structure and reaction intensity were only slightly affected by ammonia blending, demonstrating the feasibility of ammonia-blended COG for stable combustion. NOx emissions increased substantially because of enhanced fuel-NO formation. This study provides a fundamental database for ammonia-blended COG under nonpremixed conditions and can contribute to the development of low-carbon industrial combustion systems.

title: Micro-computed tomography analysis of root and canal morphology in maxillary primary molars
abstractText: Abstract Effective pulpectomy of maxillary primary molars depends on a clear understanding of their complex internal root canal anatomy, yet high-resolution data on the second mesiobuccal (MB2) canal in the primary dentition remain scarce. Using micro-computed tomography (micro-CT; SkyScan 1172; 13.61 μm isotropic voxel size), the three-dimensional root and canal morphology of 60 extracted maxillary primary molars were charaterized, focusing on the prevalence, location, and morphometry of the MB2 canal, along with inter-orifice distances, canal diameters, and dentin wall thickness. Three-rooted molars predominated (83.3%). An MB2 canal was present in 43.3% of mesiobuccal roots and, when present, was consistently located palatal to the main mesiobuccal (MB1) canal, originating predominantly in the coronal third. Long-oval and oval cross-sections together accounted for almost all canals. The MB1–MB2 inter-orifice distance was the shortest of any canal pair (mean 1.12 mm), and buccolingual diameters exceeded mesiodistal diameters in the mesiobuccal, MB2, and distobuccal roots but not the palatal root. Apical dentin was thinnest in the palatal roots (0.10 mm). Maxillary primary molars therefore combine a frequently overlooked MB2 canal with thin apical walls. These findings may help clinicians plan access cavities, select instruments, and perform conservative apical preparation during pulpectomy procedures.

Validasi menggunakan lembar penilaian skala Likert 1–5 dan hasilnya dinyatakan sebagai persentase validitas. title: Adoption of Automation and Smart Technologies in Modern Textile Production Systems
abstractText: Automation, artificial intelligence, connected sensing technologies, digital twins, robotics, and data-driven control systems are increasingly transforming textile and apparel production systems. However, in existing studies, these technologies have often been analyzed separately or limited to specific factories, countries, or specific stages of the production process. The study created an integrated analytical framework for analyzing the maturity of technology adoption in modern textile production systems, with a new dataset based on data collected from various sources related to technology adoption and digital readiness open to the public. The complete dataset contains a total of 8,198 analytical observations and 26 variables. The dataset covers nine manufacturing and business activities for the period 2019-2023 in five countries - Bangladesh, Chile, Ethiopia, India and Senegal. As part of this study, a subset of 5,472 production-based observations were used for predictive modeling. This subset is divided into 3,830 trainings, 821 validations, and 821 test observations, respectively, in a group-conscious manner. The study compared the performance of four models: Random Forest, XGBoost, Support Vector Machine and One-Dimensional Convolutional Neural Network (1D CNN). The final results showed 92.00%, 93.00%, 93.56% and 96.10% accuracy respectively, making 1D CNN the highest performing model. In a test set of 821 observations, 1D CNN's class-based F1 score was 95.29% for Basic / Manual, 97.54% for Intermediate / Mechanized, 68.57% for Digital, and 95.20% for Advanced / Smart. In the supplied ROC analysis, the value of AUC was found to be 0.998094. Integrated Gradients-based Explainable AI analysis also indicates that country-specific context, clothing cutting and sewing activities, production-domain indicators, quality-management-related variables, survey duration, and internet access rate contribute significantly to model decisions. Overall, the results show that it is possible to effectively analyze the maturity of technology adoption by combining various publicly available technology indicators with machine learning and deep learning. At the same time, class inequalities and limitations in the comparability of data from different countries have also been identified, which are important considerations for future research and external verification.

title: Cost estimate for the procurement and preparation of donated corneas for transplantation in an eye bank
abstractText: Abstract Corneal diseases are among the leading causes of blindness, and transplantation may be the only treatment option. Studies providing a comprehensive economic analysis of the corneal tissue processing chain, from procurement to release for transplantation by eye banks, are scarce. This study aimed to estimate the cost of preparing donated corneal tissue for transplantation at an Eye Bank. We performed a cost analysis using the Time-Driven Activity-Based Costing (TDABC) method based on data from the stages of corneal tissue preparation. The study population consisted of data from corneal donors collected in 2023. The median cost per donor was estimated at USD 454.65. Supplies (43%), human resources (32%), and operational costs (23%) were the costliest components. Multiple regression analysis identified predictors influencing costs. This study highlighted critical stages in the process and resource consumption. Investing in domestic pharmaceutical production, improving interinstitutional communication, training healthcare professionals, and providing logistical support may reduce costs and contribute to the management and sustainability of Eye Banks.

title: Detection-aware disparity refinement for weak-texture pavement target reconstruction in stereo vision
abstractText: Abstract Accurate detection and depth perception of pavement targets from close-range remote sensing observations are important for intelligent road monitoring and transportation infrastructure assessment. However, existing stereo matching methods often produce unstable disparity estimates in weak-texture and low-height pavement regions, such as manhole covers and speed bumps, where the disparity distribution is easily affected by matching ambiguity and image noise. To address this issue, a detection-guided disparity post-processing strategy named Detection-Aware Disparity Refinement (DADR) is proposed. A custom pavement dataset containing approximately 3000 annotated images is first constructed from a binocular vision-based remote sensing platform, covering five pavement target categories, including manhole covers, speed bumps, road damage, storm drains, and iron plates. YOLOv11 is employed to detect target regions, while FoundationStereo is used to generate initial disparity maps from calibrated stereo images. Instead of modifying the stereo matching network, the proposed method performs a rule-based post-processing operation that combines detection bounding boxes, a local ground-reference disparity, and confidence-weighted fusion to stabilize the disparity representation within detected target regions. Experimental results show that the YOLOv11 detector achieves a Precision of 0.89, a Recall of 0.88, and an mAP@50 of 0.895, and compares favourably with other one-stage detectors trained under the same protocol. Visual analysis with magnified regions of interest shows that the proposed strategy produces more spatially coherent disparity responses for weak-texture pavement targets, and an ablation study identifies the local ground reference and the adaptive confidence weighting as the main contributing components. Quantitative evaluation indicates that the within-region disparity standard deviation decreases from 3.81 px to 1.25 px after refinement. Because no independent depth ground truth is available, this result is reported as improved local disparity consistency rather than improved absolute depth accuracy. The proposed approach offers a lightweight, detector-agnostic disparity stabilization strategy for low-height pavement targets in close-range remote sensing scenarios and provides useful geometric cues for subsequent road-condition assessment, while its reliance on a locally planar ground reference and on detector reliability is discussed as a limitation.

title: Mechanistic Insights into Sodium Storage in N-Doped Graphene/MoS2 Heterostructures Revealed by Operando Raman Spectroscopy
abstractText: Abstract Two-dimensional (2D) heterostructures offer tunable interlayer spacing and accessible surfaces that can overcome key limitations of conventional sodium-ion battery (SIBs) anodes. Here, we investigate Na+ storage mechanisms in three-layer 2D heterostructures composed of horizontally stacked graphene (G), nitrogen-doped graphene (NG), and MoS2 (M) by combining cyclic voltammetry with operando spectroelectrochemical Raman spectroscopy. Restricting the active thickness to three atomic layers enables direct spectroscopic access to interfacial charge transfer and strain during cycling. Electrochemical analysis reveals that Na+ storage is governed by two coupled factors: the permeability of the electrolyte-facing outer layer, and the electronic–mechanical interactions within the interlayer space. NG outer layers facilitate ion access and deliver up to 40-fold higher capacities than pristine graphene stacks, whereas MoS2 top layers suppress ion infiltration. Operando Raman correlates faradaic features with reversible structural changes, allowing separation of charge-doping and strain effects during cycling. The results demonstrate that Na+ storage proceeds predominantly via reversible accumulation in confined interlayer and blister-like reservoirs formed during solvent cointercalation. Incorporating MoS2 as a middle layer redistributes charge and buffers mechanical strain, enhancing cycling stability. These findings provide insights into charge storage mechanisms in 2D materials.

title: Assessment of mechanical response and damage mechanisms in fly ash and basalt fiber beams strengthened with different FRP wrap configurations
abstractText: Abstract Sustainable materials and effective strengthening methods can contribute to the significant improvement of the structural performance and durability of reinforced concrete (RC) beams. 40% cement-fly ash replacement offers better sustainability and workability, whereas fibre reinforcement and external fibre reinforced polymer (FRP) wrapping are able to offer better strength and ductility. This paper is an experimental study where thirteen RC beams were studied, one of them being a conventional control beam, basalt fibre reinforced beam (BFRB) fibre contents of 0.5%, 1%, 1.5%, 2% and beams strengthened by applying E-glass fibre reinforced polymer (EGFRP) wraps, and glass fibre reinforced polymer (GFRP) wraps at 50, 75, 100, and 150 mm. In all mixes of concrete, fly ash was used as a partial replacement of cement (12.5%). The beams were tested to assess the load–deflection response, stiffness, ductility, cracking and failure modes. The mid-span deflections were determined analytically and the deflection was determined by the double integration method, which was compared to the experimental results. Basalt fibre content was found to result in much higher load-carrying capacity, stiffness, ductility and crack control than in the control beam, and a 1.5% of basalt fibre gave the best balance between strength and deformation capacity. A higher fibre dosage of 2.0% resulted in reduced performance due to fibre agglomeration. External FRP wrapping further improved beam performance, with closer wrapping spacings (50 and 75 mm) offering superior confinement and crack-bridging effects. GFRP wrapping consistently outperformed EGFRP, and the GFRP-wrapped beam with 1.5% basalt fibre and 100 mm spacing achieved the highest load capacity and deflection. As a whole, the obtained results showed that the concrete beams can be reinforced with the observed load conditions by applying the combination of fly ash, basalt fibres and external FRP wrapping.

abstractText: This study aims to analyze the influence of swimming pool entertainment facilities on guest satisfaction at AHA Hotel. The study employed a quantitative approach supported by qualitative data. A total of 97 respondents were selected using purposive sampling and the Cochran formula. Data were collected through a five-point Likert-scale questionnaire, observation, semi-structured interviews, and documentation. The swimming pool entertainment facilities variable was measured based on servicescape indicators, while guest satisfaction was measured based on the comparison between guests’ expectations and their actual experiences. Data were analyzed using descriptive analysis and simple linear regression. The results showed that the swimming pool entertainment facilities obtained an overall mean score of 3.92, which was categorized as good. The highest-rated indicator was the attractiveness of the swimming pool facilities, with a mean score of 4.04, while the lowest score was found for pool water cleanliness, at 3.75. Guest satisfaction obtained an overall mean score of 3.61 and was also categorized as good. The t-test results showed a calculated t-value of 10.671 > the t-table value of 1.661, with a significance value of 0.000 < 0.05, indicating that swimming pool entertainment facilities have a positive and significant effect on guest satisfaction. The correlation coefficient of 0.738 indicates a strong relationship, while the R² value of 0.545 indicates that swimming pool entertainment facilities contribute 54.5% to the variation in guest satisfaction. These findings highlight the importance of sustainable facility management, particularly in improving water cleanliness, the availability of supporting facilities, facility maintenance, and the quality of guests’ recreational experiences.

abstractText: Abstract Introduction Structurally vulnerable patients experience worse health outcomes, exacerbated by healthcare workers’ negative attitudes and limited understanding of structural barriers to care. Structural competency may improve attitudes towards structurally vulnerable patients, but the impact on attitudes and practices has not been rigorously evaluated, particularly in clinical settings. Methods Medical students at Weill Cornell Medical College in New York City participated in a structural competency-informed curriculum aligned with transformative learning theory which incorporates clinical skills training with simulation and reflection during academic years 2022–2023 and 2023–2024. Authors conducted a convergent mixed-methods study using pre-post surveys and thematic analysis of reflections to explore if and how the curriculum impacted students’ attitudes and practices towards structurally vulnerable patients. Surveys included the Medical Condition Regard Scale (MCRS) and items accessing self-efficacy in applying the curriculum’s learning objectives. Results Of 190 students, 77 (40.5%) completed the pre-survey and 50 (26.3%) completed pre- and post-surveys. The mean pre-course MCRS score ( n = 50) was 4.18/6 (SD 0.79) and the mean post-course MCRS score was 4.57/6 (SD 0.75), showing a mean increase of 0.39 (SD 0.49, t-test P < 0.001, Cohen’s d = 0.81). Thematic analysis of 21 reflections identified four themes highlighting how students employed patient-centered communication strategies, utilized best practices in discharge planning, engaged in critical self-reflection and reframing, and appreciated how structural barriers shape health. Conclusion Findings suggest that integrating education on structural factors with clinical skills training, reinforced through simulation and reflection, can improve self-reported attitudes and perceived self-efficacy in caring for structurally vulnerable patients.
